title: How mobile networks work
examples: How far can a cell tower send a signal?
What is the difference between 4G and 5G?
Do I need a cell tower to use my phone?

explain.say: A cell tower is a tall structure that helps send signals.
These towers broadcast signals using invisible radio waves.
Radio waves travel through the air very quickly to your phone.
4G networks provide fast data for streaming and video calls.
5G is the newest generation, offering even faster speeds and lower delays.
In real life, when you are in a basement, the signal is weak.

faq.q: How far can a cell tower send a signal?
faq.a: The range depends on the tower's power and the surrounding buildings. Sometimes you need multiple towers working together.
asks: Does signal strength change with distance?

faq.q: What is the main difference between 4G and 5G?
faq.a: The main difference is speed and capacity. 5G can handle more devices and transfer data much faster than 4G.
asks: What does 'low latency' mean for my phone?

faq.q: Do I need a cell tower to use my phone?
faq.a: You need a cell tower or a network connection to send or receive calls and data. If there is no tower, you cannot connect.
asks: Can I use my phone offline?
What happens if there is no signal?

faq.q: Are radio waves safe to use with phones?
faq.a: The radio waves used by mobile networks are a type of non-ionizing radiation. They are regulated by safety standards.
asks: Are phone signals harmful to health?
What kind of energy are radio waves?

faq.a: Latency is the delay before a transfer of data begins following an instruction. Lower latency means a faster, more immediate response.
asks: Why is low latency important for video calls?

facts: Cell towers use antennas to broadcast radio waves.
Radio waves are a form of electromagnetic energy.
5G networks are designed for much higher data speeds than 4G.
Signal strength can be reduced by thick walls or underground areas.

quiz.say: A tall structure sending signals is called a:
quiz.why: A cell tower is the physical structure that broadcasts the network signal.

wrong.1: An antenna is just one part of the tower, not the whole structure.
wrong.2: A radio wave is the invisible energy that travels, not the source.
wrong.3: A base station is a general term, but 'cell tower' is the common name for the whole unit.

quiz.say: If you are streaming a high-definition video, which network is better:
quiz.why: 5G offers significantly higher bandwidth and faster speeds needed for HD streaming.

wrong.0: 4G might work, but it could buffer or lag during high-definition streaming.
wrong.1: Signal strength is about power, not the underlying network technology (4G vs 5G).
wrong.2: The height does not determine the maximum data speed available.

quiz.say: When signal strength drops because of thick concrete, this is an example of:
quiz.why: Physical objects like concrete absorb or weaken the radio waves as they pass through.

wrong.1: Frequency shift means the wave changes its pitch, which is not what happens here.
wrong.2: Reflection is bouncing off surfaces, but concrete causes absorption/weakening.
wrong.3: Bandwidth is the capacity, not the physical weakening caused by materials.
